title: IELTS Academic Reading — Full-Length Original Practice
description: Unofficial original practice: three passages, 40 questions, and 60 minutes. This is not an official IELTS test.

reading.instructions: Answer all 40 questions. Use evidence in each passage; the practice uses the teacher review workflow.

passages.title: Heat below the streets
passages.content:
The fictional city of Norhaven tested district heating as a way to reuse heat that would otherwise be lost. Its engineers compared several neighbourhoods before recommending a cautious expansion.

The first pilot connected the riverside clinic to a heat network in 2018. Engineers used insulated pipes to carry hot water beneath the pavement. A data centre supplied waste heat during the winter trial. The library joined the network only after a separate heat exchanger was installed. Measurements showed lower gas use in connected buildings, but the report did not compare construction costs. The team found that older pipes lost more heat at shallow joints. A maintenance crew inspected the network every six weeks. Residents received notices before work began on each street. The council paused expansion until a second winter of data had been collected. The pilot used water at a lower temperature than the city’s older steam system. A university group checked the temperature sensors independently. The report recommended mapping underground utilities before selecting new routes. The researchers warned that savings would vary with building insulation.

passages.title: A night sky with fewer lamps
passages.content:
In the fictional district of Bellmere, planners studied whether street lighting could be reduced without making paths feel unsafe. The team combined light measurements with interviews and a small controlled trial.

The survey covered twelve streets beside the town’s canal. Researchers measured brightness at pavement level rather than at lamp height. The trial replaced broad white lamps with shielded amber lights. The shield directed most light toward the walkway and away from bedroom windows. Participants walked each route at the same time on three evenings. The interviews found that even lighting mattered more to many walkers than maximum brightness. A separate group checked the routes during rainy weather. The trial reduced electricity use by about one fifth on the selected streets. The study recorded no change in reported falls during its short trial. The authors said the trial was too brief to establish long-term accident rates. Shop owners asked that signs near crossings remain clearly illuminated. The planners advised testing each lamp design with local residents before wider use. The report treated light pollution and personal safety as separate measures.

passages.title: Seeds kept for uncertain seasons
passages.content:
A fictional agricultural institute built a seed collection to help farms prepare for changing rainfall. Its researchers stress that stored seeds are useful only when their origins and growing conditions are recorded.

The collection began with seeds from farms in three neighbouring valleys. Each packet received a code linked to its collection location and date. Staff dried the seeds slowly before placing them in sealed containers. A temperature log showed that the storage room stayed near four degrees Celsius. The institute tested a small sample from every new batch for germination. Some local varieties germinated later but survived longer without irrigation. Researchers compared growth in sandy soil and heavier clay soil. The trial did not identify one variety that performed best in every field. Farmers helped choose which traits to measure during the growing season. The institute returned duplicate seed samples to two village cooperatives. A yearly inventory was introduced after several labels became difficult to read. The report recommends keeping a living field collection alongside frozen storage. Researchers cautioned that a seed collection cannot replace healthy soils or reliable water. The next trial will compare planting dates after an unusually dry spring.
